Waube is an endangered indigenous language of Papua New Guinea. It belongs to the Trans-New Guinea language family. The language is used as a first language by all adults in the ethnic community, but not all young people. It is not known to be taught in schools. The music of Papua New Guinea encompasses a wide range of traditional and contemporary styles developed across the country's highly diverse ethnic groups. Traditional celebrations known as sing-sing feature communal song and dance, and form a central part of cultural life. At ceremonial dances men and women play hour-glass drums and blow whistles in time with their dance movements and sung messages. At collective courting occasions, people sing songs and courting pairs turn their heads together expressively in time with the singing.
